deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page is a working draft of §§7–9 of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe' (written 1854, published 1867). The previous page belongs to the historical introduction (Lagrange, Fourier, Cauchy, Dirichlet). The next page treats the example f = d(x^nu cos(1/x))/dx and a stationary-phase computation (§13).

The setting is the series Omega = A0 + A1 + A2 + ..., with A0 = b0/2 and A_n = a_n sin nx + b_n cos nx (published notation).

(1) Case split. A necessary condition for convergence is that the terms tend to 0. Riemann separates two cases: (I) the terms A_n(x) -> 0 for every x, i.e. a_n, b_n -> 0; (II) this happens only for special x.

(2) Case I: the twice-integrated series. Integrating Omega termwise twice gives
F(x) = p + q x + (1/4) b0 x^2 - A1/1 - A2/4 - A3/9 - ...
Here (1/4) b0 x^2 = A0 x^2/2. Since the A_n are bounded, sum A_n/n^2 converges uniformly, so F converges for every x and is continuous. This justification is mine; Riemann only states the conclusion.

(3) First lemma (published Satz 1). If Omega converges at x, then
[F(x+a+b) - F(x-a+b) - F(x+a-b) + F(x-a-b)]/(4ab)
tends to the sum of the series as a, b -> 0 with a/b bounded.
Computation (partly mine, partly in the fragments at the foot of the page):
- For each term A_n(x), the four-point difference equals -4 sin(na) sin(nb) A_n(x). This rests on cos n(a+b) - cos n(a-b) = -2 sin(na) sin(nb), which is the bottom line 'A_n cos n(a+b) - cos n(a-b)'.
- The fragment '-2A_n cos n(x+b) + 2A_n cos n(x-b)' is an intermediate step of the same calculation.
- The quadratic term gives (A0/2)·8ab, so after division by 4ab it contributes A0. The linear part cancels.
- Hence the quotient equals A0 + sum_n A_n (sin na/(na))(sin nb/(nb)).
- The step from convergence of Omega to convergence of this weighted sum (summability by these kernels) is not written on the page. In the published version it is done by Abel summation.

Conclusion drawn on the page: representability of f by a trigonometric series requires a continuous F whose generalized second difference quotient equals f. This is not sufficient, so the problem becomes finding conditions on F for the equation
lim_{a->0} [F(x+a) - 2F(x) + F(x-a)]/a^2 = series.

(4) Integral representation of the partial sums (published §9). Formally f(x+t) + f(x-t) is expanded as a cosine series in t, with coefficients the A_n(x). The partial sum A0 + ... + A_n is then expressed, after two integrations by parts, as
(1/pi) ∫_0^pi (F(x+t) + F(x-t) - 2F(x)) · d^2/dt^2 [sin((2n+1)t/2)/sin(t/2)] dt, with n -> ∞.
The kernel is the second t-derivative of the Dirichlet kernel; the written '∂t²' belongs to it, it is not a square. The orthogonality check: the even part of F(x+t) contains -(A_k/k^2) cos kt, and D_n'' = -2 sum k^2 cos kt, so the integral returns 2pi A_k over [-pi, pi].

(5) Localization (published Satz 3). For this equation to hold, the contribution of every interval not containing x (including its endpoints) must tend to 0 as n -> ∞. The limit of the integral is then independent of the values of F(t) at finite distance from x. Thus convergence at x depends only on the behaviour of F near x.

(6) Marginal notes:
- A statement of the Cauchy criterion: by continuing the series far enough, its fluctuations under further continuation can be confined to arbitrarily narrow bounds.
- The termwise integration formula ∫_a^b f dx = ∫_a^b f1 dx + ∫_a^b f2 dx + ... .
- A restatement of 'I. Fall: terms -> 0 for every x', with stray coefficient fragments (-b_n cos mx cos n(x+b) + a_m sin mx cos n(x+b)), apparently a product-to-sum attempt.
errors: The formal expansion is written as f(x+t)+f(x-t) = ½A0 + ΣA_n cos nt. With A0 = b0/2 the correct normalization is 2A0 + 2Σ A_n(x) cos nt. This is a draft-level normalization slip.
The integral ∫^π ... dt omits the factor 1/π (or 1/(2π) over [-π,π]). The lower limit is not written.

The passage from convergence of Ω to convergence of A0 + Σ A_n (sin nα/nα)(sin nβ/nβ) is asserted without proof here. It needs the Abel-summation argument of the published §8 together with the boundedness of α/β.
Continuity and convergence of F are asserted without justification on the page. They follow from uniform convergence of ΣA_n/n² given bounded coefficients.
The bottom-line fragments (mixing indices m and n) are unfinished scratch work, not a correct formula as written.

results.what: Case distinction: coefficients a_n,b_n -> 0 (terms vanish for every x) versus terms vanishing only at special x
results.modern_name: Preliminary to the Cantor–Lebesgue theorem setting
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Habilitationsschrift 1854/1867); Cantor 1870 for the Cantor–Lebesgue theorem

results.what: F = twice termwise integrated series is continuous; its symmetric second difference quotient [F(x+α+β)-F(x-α+β)-F(x+α-β)+F(x-α-β)]/(4αβ) tends to the sum of Ω where Ω converges
results.modern_name: Riemann's first lemma (Riemann summability / Schwarz second symmetric derivative)

results.what: Representation of partial sums via ∫(F(x+t)+F(x-t)-2F(x)) d²/dt²[Dirichlet kernel] dt
results.modern_name: Riemann's integral formula for partial sums in terms of the second integral

results.what: Convergence at x depends only on the behaviour of F (hence f) in a neighbourhood of x
Fluctuation of a series under further continuation can be made arbitrarily small

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of §§7–9 of Riemann's published Habilitationsschrift: Satz 1 with exactly the 4αβ formulation, the integral formula of §9, and the localization principle, all well known as his. Its only interest is as a working draft showing variants (the α-only second difference, normalization slips).

checkable.asserts: Four-point difference of cos n x equals -4 sin(na) sin(nb) cos(nx) (should simplify to 0)
Same identity for sin n x (should be 0)
Quadratic term A0 x^2/2 contributes exactly A0 (result 1)
Bottom-line fragment: cos n(α+β) - cos n(α-β) = -2 sin nα sin nβ (should be 0)

checkable.sympy: integrate(-cos(3*t)/9 * diff(1 + 2*sum(cos(k*t) for k in range(1,6)), t, 2), (t, -pi, pi))
checkable.asserts: Kernel D_n'' picks out coefficient: term -(A_k/k^2) cos kt (k=3, A_k=1) integrates to 2*pi
Kernel weights tend to 1 as α->0 (result 1)

transcription_corrections: The kernel in the integral is most likely ∂²/∂t² (sin((2n+1)t/2)/sin(t/2)), with '∂t²' as the denominator of the second derivative, not the square of the Dirichlet kernel. The stray '{+t^2 [?]+}' in the transcription is this ∂t² of the kernel.
The '50' at the right margin is the folio number, not part of the formula.
'Fx+α+β …' in the sentence on representability is Riemann's abbreviation for the full four-term difference quotient over 4αβ.
The first term '{+zu+} {+nicht so direct+}' is a marginal note above the first line.
'Dies vorausgesetzt' refers to Case I (coefficients tending to zero); the series for Fx reads p + qx + ¼b₀x² − A₁/1 − A₂/4 − …, consistent with A₀ = b₀/2.
